reflection: Results are not visible in this run, so I rely on priors. The useful existing factors are volatility, MSFT_return_1d and longer-horizon trend, which points to volatility-regime and peer-move features. I will try variants of volatility ratios and peer-relative signals that are smoother and less noisy. I will also try a few new ideas based on volume and on the range relative to the market.

factors.name: aapl_vol5_to_vol20_log
factors.hypothesis: The 10d/20d ratio overlaps heavily with existing vol factors. Using a 5d window against a 60d baseline captures short-term vol spikes that tend to mean-revert, with less redundancy.

factors.name: msft_return_zscore_60d_clipped
factors.hypothesis: MSFT_return_1d is useful, but the 20d z-score is noisy. A 60d window gives a steadier standardized MSFT shock that is comparable across volatility regimes.

factors.name: qqq_range_vs_aapl_range
factors.formula: subtract(safe_divide(subtract(QQQ_High, QQQ_Low), QQQ_Close), safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_High, AAPL_Low), AAPL_Close))
factors.hypothesis: The gap between market range and Apple range shows whether Apple's volatility is idiosyncratic. Idiosyncratic spikes may revert differently from market-wide ones.

factors.name: aapl_volume_change_x_return_5d
factors.hypothesis: A 5-day move accompanied by a rising volume ratio signals conviction or exhaustion. This is a nonlinear interaction the tree model can use.

factors.name: nvda_msft_mean_return_3d_minus_aapl
factors.hypothesis: Pairs with the vol-regime factor. Whether Apple lags recent peer strength matters more when vol is elevated, because catch-up or reversal is stronger.

factors.name: qqq_close_to_ma60_trend
factors.hypothesis: Gives the medium-term market trend regime. It conditions how a MSFT shock carries over to Apple, which may differ between bull and bear regimes.
